title: Scanner page -- run a scan, review candidates, add hits to the watchlist
description: A new page, not a section of the watchlist or ticker detail view (per docs/ideas.md's own scoping): pick a scan category, run it, review the resulting candidate list, and add any worth tracking to the watchlist (POST /api/watchlist, already built) -- each hit's drill-down is the existing ticker detail view. Must clearly show a disabled/unavailable state (not an error) when IBKR isn't connected, consistent with the backend's own degrade-gracefully contract.

checklist.step: Build a new Scanner page: category picker, a 'run scan' action, and a results list with each hit linking to the ticker detail view (TickerLink) and an 'add to watchlist' action per row.
Show a clear, non-error disabled state when the backend reports IBKR unavailable/disabled.
Add the page to app navigation.
Component tests covering: available with results, available with zero results, and the disabled/unavailable state.

decisions.decision: New common/UnavailableState component (with its own Storybook stories + test) renders the 'the feature is disabled/not reachable right now, nothing is actually broken' case -- distinct from both common/ErrorState (genuine ApiError, red/alert styling, role="alert") and common/EmptyState (real data, just zero of it). ScannerPage renders it whenever GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params's state !== 'available'; ScannerPanel renders it again for the same non-'available' outcome from POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run (reachable if IBKR drops between the params check and the run). This is the first frontend feature that needs to distinguish this three-way split (broken / disabled-but-fine / empty-but-fine) since this is the first UI built against any of the /api/ibkr/* routes.
decisions.rationale: Reusing EmptyState for the disabled state was rejected: this task's own checklist explicitly calls out 'available with zero results' and 'the disabled/unavailable state' as two scenarios a reviewer needs to be able to tell apart at a glance, and EmptyState's framing ('no data to show you') is a poor fit for 'this data source can't even be reached right now' -- conflating them under one component/message would blur exactly the distinction the checklist calls out. Reusing ErrorState (e.g. by synthesizing a fake ApiError for a 200 response) was also rejected: `disabled`/`gateway_unreachable`/`not_authenticated` are deliberately not ApiErrors at all (API.md, backend-market-scanner's own decisions) precisely so the frontend doesn't have to render them as failures -- forcing them through ErrorState's alert-role/red-icon treatment would fight that contract and require inventing a synthetic error object for something that isn't one. A new, small, genuinely reusable common component (no domain knowledge, just heading+optional message) was the cleaner fit and will likely be reused once frontend-ibkr-status-indicator (still planned) needs the same treatment.

decisions.decision: The category picker only exposes IBKR's own scan-type `code`/`display_name` (GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params's `categories`, normalized via features/scanner/scannerCategories.ts's `toScannerCategories`). `scan_config`'s `instrument`/`location` fields are hardcoded to `'STK'`/`'STK.US.MAJOR'` (the exact defaults `IBKRScannerRunRequest.scan_config`'s own schema `examples` document) rather than exposed as further pickers.
decisions.rationale: GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params's backend handler only ever forwards IBKR's `scan_type_list` -- it deliberately discards `instrument_list`/`location_tree` entirely (see backend-market-scanner's own decisions entry: 'passing through the raw scan_type_list... rather than hand-curating'), so there is no server-exposed option list this frontend could build an instrument/location picker from without inventing one client-side from scratch (duplicating gateway-versioned option data the backend explicitly chose not to model, for the same staleness-risk reason that task gave). Building a full instrument/location/filter-builder UI is also out of scope for this task's own 'pick a scan category, run it' framing (task description) -- that is a materially larger feature (a generic scan-config form) than what was asked for here. STK/STK.US.MAJOR was chosen over any other fixed pair specifically because it's the literal example the backend schema itself documents, not a value invented for this task.

decisions.decision: ScannerResultsTable imports and reuses features/watchlist/hooks/useAddWatchlistItem.ts directly for its per-row 'Add to watchlist' action, rather than writing a second POST /api/watchlist mutation hook under features/scanner/hooks/. This is the first cross-feature hook import in the codebase (every prior feature's hooks are only ever consumed from within that same feature's own components/pages).
decisions.rationale: useAddWatchlistItem already encapsulates the correct behavior end to end (idempotent no-op on a duplicate add per API.md, invalidates watchlist queries on success) -- duplicating it under features/scanner/hooks/ would risk the two implementations silently drifting (e.g. one gaining a bug fix or an invalidation the other doesn't). Frontend.md §3's placement rules explicitly restrict *component* placement (`components/common/` vs `features/<domain>/components/`, checked by pr-reviewer) but say nothing about restricting a mutation hook -- a thin wrapper over one `useMutation` call with no feature-specific rendering -- to only being called from within its own feature. Considered lifting `useAddWatchlistItem` (or the underlying `addWatchlistItem` API call) into a shared, feature-agnostic location instead; rejected since it already lives exactly where Frontend.md's hook-placement rule says a watchlist-domain hook belongs ('features/portfolio/hooks/usePortfolio.ts... lives under the feature it serves'), and moving it would only be justified if a third consumer made the watchlist feature itself feel like the wrong owner -- not yet the case here.

decisions.decision: common/ErrorState gained a fourth documented status case (429, alongside 404/422/503/0): a distinct 'Too many requests' heading/icon, plus a new `Try again in {retryAfterSeconds}s.` line rendered when `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds` is non-null. Previously 429 fell through to the generic 'Something went wrong' default case, since no earlier frontend feature had ever called a rate-limited backend route (POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run is the first).
decisions.rationale: API.md documents 429 as a real, expected outcome of POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run (IBKRProvider's 1-request/second client-side throttle) and api/client.ts already parses the response's Retry-After header into `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds` specifically so a caller doesn't have to -- leaving ErrorState's generic fallback in place for this endpoint's very first UI consumer would both mislabel a normal, actionable, retry-shortly outcome as 'Something went wrong' and leave that already-parsed retry delay unused. Rendering the retry delay as its own Typography line (not appended into `detail`'s string) was chosen so a future backend wording change to `detail` can never accidentally duplicate or contradict this app-owned line.

comments.summary: Blocking: ScannerResultsTable shares a single useAddWatchlistItem() mutation instance across every row's 'Add to watchlist' button. TanStack Query's MutationObserver.mutate() detaches the observer from whatever mutation it was previously watching before attaching to the new one, so clicking a second row's Add button before the first row's request settles means the first row's onSuccess (and isError/ErrorState) never fires once its request does complete -- its button stays stuck on 'Add to watchlist' even though the ticker really was added server-side. Independently reproduced with an instrumented test (two staggered POST /api/watchlist calls, both resolve successfully, only 1 of 2 rows ever flips to 'Added'). Root cause: one useAddWatchlistItem() call shared by the whole table instead of one per row (or reconciling addedTickers against a source of truth independent of the shared mutation's own variables/onSuccess).

Non-blocking: no Playwright e2e spec was added for the new /scanner page under frontend/tests/e2e/ -- the existing 18 specs (all still pass, no regression) don't exercise the scanner golden path (category -> run -> results -> add-to-watchlist) or its disabled state at the persisted-regression layer, which the e2e-test skill's own docs call out as expected companion work for a new UI flow. Tracked as a follow-up.

review.notes: Full review: backend unaffected (pytest 1139 passed, 99.95% coverage; ruff/mypy clean); frontend vitest 741 passed, 99.7%+ coverage across all four metrics; yarn lint/tsc/build/build-storybook all clean; own Playwright walkthrough against the real dev server covered the disabled state, golden path (category picker -> run -> results incl. the no-symbol #<conid> fallback -> add to watchlist -> Added), and the 429/Retry-After edge case, all rendering correctly with no console errors; make e2e's 18 existing specs all pass (no scanner-specific spec exists, see non-blocking finding); component placement (common/UnavailableState vs features/scanner/* ) correctly follows Frontend.md Sec.3, and all four recorded decisions are sound with real rejected alternatives. The one blocking finding is the shared-mutation bug in ScannerResultsTable (see comments) -- a real, easily user-reachable race (clicking Add on two different scan results before the first completes), not an edge case. An earlier PR comment from this same review pass called this cosmetic and posted 'accepted' before the code-review skill's parallel pass (independently reproduced here) surfaced the fuller, blocking version of the same root cause -- that earlier comment is superseded by this verdict.
